lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs' season is in the books at 32-36-14, and the conversation has moved squarely to what comes next. They finished 8th in atlantic division - a final placement that frames every decision this summer. The work now runs through the draft table, the trade market and the cap sheet, and the bets made over the next few weeks will shape the roster that shows up to camp. The next headline here comes from the front office, not the scoreboard. The NHL calendar has flipped to building season - draft prep, trade talks, and the roster surgery that shapes the next contending window. For the Toronto Maple Leafs, the work runs from the draft table to the trade market, and the choices made this summer will define the next window.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays keep finding new ways to make a loud mess of a promising week - some fight, a few flashes, and then another loss to remind everyone where they stand. Tuesday's 7-4 defeat to the Phillies dropped Toronto to 33-36, third in the AL East and nine games back, a record that leaves no room for self-deception even after the 3-2 win the night before and the 6-4 victory over Baltimore on Saturday. Max Scherzer gave the club a headline anyway, ringing up his 3,500th career strikeout, a milestone that belongs in a museum even if the outing itself did not rescue the afternoon. The veteran has become the story inside the story: still working, still defiant, still chasing history while the lineup asks for more than scattered bursts. Toronto is 1-3 in its last four, and the run has the feel of a team that can hang around but not yet take the wheel. Now comes Friday night in New York against the Yankees - another test, another chance to prove this slump is a detour, not a verdict.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The spring ended with the Raptors where too many middling teams land - good enough to matter, not good enough to scare anyone. At 46-36 and third in the Atlantic, they squeezed value from a season that still demanded more, and the hard truth is that a one-game finish never hides a larger problem: this roster needs a clearer spine. Raptors commit to Bobby Webster's vision with a long-term extension is the most telling move of the moment; ownership has chosen a direction, and now the basketball has to match it. The draft board already points that way, with Bennett Stirtz drawing attention as the kind of underdog point guard who can steady a possession and Hannes Steinbach offering the stretch-big profile this team has lacked. That matters because the roster has too often lived on fragments - useful parts, not a finished machine. The next months will tell us whether this was a decent pause or the start of something sturdier. What comes next is the real test: a sharp draft, practical center shopping, and no more drifting in the middle.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: Something is taking shape at Ashburn, and it isn't smoke - it's hierarchy. Joshua Josephs has pushed himself into the conversation in the final week of OTAs, while Luke McCaffrey and Mikey Sainristil keep pressing their cases and making this roster feel less settled than it looked a month ago. That is the real summer story for a club that finished 3rd in the NFC East, 6 games back, with a W1 finish to a season that is over and done with. The old comfort blanket of "prove it in camp" is gone; now every rep matters for the young players trying to grab a job and for the veterans trying to keep one. McCaffrey, once the forgotten wideout, is finally forcing coaches to look twice. Sainristil, meanwhile, is shaping up as more than a nice depth piece - he looks like a defender ready to matter. And the Brandon Aiyuk noise only sharpens the pressure on the receiving room. Watch minicamp for who keeps rising when the pads stay off and the pecking order starts to harden.
